articles.title: Meta says Muse has over 10M users, with shopping a top activity | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Meta Muse users are adopting the app for shopping and personal productivity, the company said during its Q3 earnings call. The AI app now has over 10M users.
articles.body_text: Meta said during its third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday that its AI app Muse has been adopted by more than 10 million users, confirming estimates released earlier this week by market intelligence firm Sensor Tower. But it is how people are using it and how much they’re spending that has caught CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s attention. Zuckerberg said about 25% of people who set up Muse now use it daily, helping improve retention. He also shared that over a quarter of Muse’s engaged users who were shopping via the AI agent had an average purchase size of over $200, which was surprising even to industry insiders. “Plaid told us that they hadn’t seen activity like they’re seeing with their connector on any other service before,” Zuckerberg said, referring to the financial technology company that connects payment apps to customers’ bank accounts. Muse uses Plaid’s connector to enable agentic shopping. Now that Muse has achieved “product-market fit,” Zuckerberg said Meta’s focus will shift to scaling the AI agent, increasing revenue, and optimizing its compute costs. Remarkably, the tech company is forecasting that Muse will eventually bring in more revenue per user than its “family of apps” users do today — meaning its users on Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger. Currently, that figure is around “several hundreds of dollars annually,” Zuckerberg said. Meta has said it ultimately intends to monetize Muse by keeping it free for most users but keeping a percentage of the commerce taking place on the platform. Power users who want access to the most advanced AI models or more tokens will also have to pay. Zuckerberg also noted that Meta believes Muse will be profitable after it scales. “On the compute side, we are building out the capacity to serve more than a billion people over the next few years,” he told bankers and analysts on the Q3 earnings call. “In the near term, Muse is very compute-intensive to run, but we expect to improve its cost efficiency by more than 10x in the next year, which will enable it to be profitable once the revenue lines are at scale.” Muse will also play a central role in Meta’s smart glasses strategy. Reality Labs, the division responsible for smart glasses, VR, and the metaverse, is still losing billions. However, the division’s losses are expected to improve from $19.1 billion in 2025 to $15 billion this year. Beyond scaling and supporting its hardware strategy, Zuckerberg teased the company’s plans for something he called the “Muse network.” He described this as taking Muse from a “single-player game” to one where “your Muses can work with your friends’ and your families’ [Muses].” “And if you want to buy something, it’s not just navigating to that business’s website; it’s talking to their agent,” he added. articles.title: Year-old AI lab Flapping Airplanes raises $1B at a $6B valuation | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Just 9 months after raising a $180 million seed round, Flapping Airplanes has landed a $1 billion Series A for its mission to build AI models "without ingesting half the internet."
articles.body_text: Year-old startup Flapping Airplanes has wowed Silicon Valley with an impressive founding team and a mission to find ways to train large models with less data. On Wednesday, the company announced it had raised a $1 billion Series A round, co-led by Index and Lux, reportedly at a $6 billion valuation. The round comes just nine months after the company launched with a $180 million seed round from GV, Sequoia, and Index. That seed round had valued the company at $1.5 billion, so its valuation just quadrupled. Other participants in the new round included earlier backers Sequoia, GV, and Kleiner Perkins. Valor, Atreides, Kleiner Perkins, A*, and Nvidia are also investors in the company. Flapping Airplanes was founded by Aidan Smith and brothers Asher and Ben Spector. Smith is a former founder and Thiel fellow who worked at the brain implant company Neuralink during college. Asher Spector was a statistics PhD at Stanford, while Ben Spector was a computer science PhD student at Stanford and founded Prod while at MIT. Prod is an almost secret-society, five-year-old student-run startup accelerator that has “become one of the most powerful talent incubators in Silicon Valley,” wrote Sequoia partner David Cahn , a Flapping Planes investor, in a post earlier this year explaining why he invested. Together, the founders “are building the ‘young person’s AGI lab,’” as Cahn described it. The founders describe their work as “the world’s most complete megakernel framework. It can perform entire training runs, serve inference, play video games, and even do all three simultaneously in a single kernel.” (A kernel is a program that runs on a GPU, and a megakernel bundles many tasks into one program.) The founders claim the framework “can overlap memory-bound inference with compute-bound training,” meaning it can run a task that spends most of its time waiting for data to be fetched alongside one that spends most of its time doing math, so the chip is rarely sitting idle. The premise is that AI has barely scratched the surface of what GPUs can do, and they believe it can create intelligent systems “without ingesting half the internet.” The goal is systems that cost less to train and run. “A model that’s a million times more data efficient is probably a million times easier to put into the economy,” Asher Spector told TechCrunch shortly after the startup launched. They now have a fresh $1 billion to hire and attempt to turn that goal into reality. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Tesla starts Optimus robot production in California as profit falls 43% | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Tesla's revenue was flat and its expenses skyrocketed as it pressed the accelerator on its Optimus robots, AI, and autonomous driving.
articles.body_text: Tesla has started production of its Optimus humanoid robot at its factory in Fremont, California, in a manufacturing space once dedicated to making electric vehicles, the company announced Wednesday. “The bots coming off this line are the first production-quality bots that we have manufactured,” Tesla wrote in its third-quarter letter to shareholders. “While we will continue to iterate on the hardware and manufacturing process, we have proven that the current manufacturing process for Optimus is suitable for a commercial product.” Tesla CEO Elon Musk said on a conference call that he considers this “early production” and that the ramp will be slow and “somewhat bumpy because it is such a radically new product.” He nonetheless claimed Tesla will be able to make 20,000 of them per week by the end of 2027. “There’s still some things we need to tweak about the design, because you need to deliver a robot that is safe and reliable and has long duration, so it can’t, like, wear out after a month,” he said. “And there’s still quite a lot of work to do with regard to the AI and the robot for it to be truly useful for open-ended tasks.” That forward-looking development wasn’t enough to lift the company’s otherwise middling third-quarter earnings, results that typify a company in the midst of a major bet. Tesla’s revenue was flat and its expenses skyrocketed as it pressed the accelerator on its Optimus robots, AI, and autonomous driving. The end result was a 43% drop in profits. The company’s revenue was largely driven by EV sales, which were flat year-over-year at $20 billion. Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, about 6,000 more than the previous quarter, but fewer than in the same period last year. Tesla’s total third-quarter revenue was $28.04 billion, a skosh below the $28.09 billion it generated in the third quarter of 2025. Tesla’s third-quarter revenue was also about $200 million lower than the previous quarter’s haul of $28.23 billion. Tesla saw a 16% year-over-year decline in revenue from its solar and energy storage business to $2.8 billion, which it blamed on tariff-related customer refunds. There was some positive revenue growth in its services business, a category that includes customer subscriptions to its Full Self-Driving advanced driver-assistance software. Tesla’s services business grew 33% year-over-year, bringing in $4.6 billion and accounting for a record $734 million in gross profit for the quarter. None of this was enough to outpace Tesla’s spending on artificial intelligence projects and its Optimus robot, which took a big bite out of profits. The company reported $787 million in net income, a 43% drop from the same period in 2025, when it earned $1.37 billion. Lower regulatory credit sales also put pressure on its profitability. “We suspect somewhere around Q2 next year is when we can turn on some of the first customer vehicles to be part of the robotaxi fleet,” Elluswamy said, referring to when privately owned Tesla vehicles equipped with FSD (Supervised) would receive a software update enabling unsupervised driving. Musk said during the company’s earnings call in April that the unsupervised version would “probably” be released in the fourth quarter of this year.

articles.title: Recursive launches Flint, a laptop coding model it says was largely built by AI | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Startup Recursive has released Flint, a free, laptop-sized coding model built largely by its own AI research system, as an early test of AI that improves itself.
articles.body_text: Recursive , an AI startup founded last year, is starting to live up to its name. The company, which is trying to build AI that can improve itself, released its first model, Flint , on Wednesday. Flint is a free coding model that can run on a laptop and was built largely with the help of AI. Recursive’s automated research system, which it calls the Eureka Machine, helped with nearly every step of Flint’s development, the company says. That let a small team build the model from scratch in under four months. Flint is an early public test of recursive self-improvement: the idea that AI can build better AI, which in turn builds even better AI. It’s also one of the most debated ideas in the industry. Some researchers fear that AI improving itself could slip out of human control. For now, Recursive’s version is more limited: an AI research assistant overseen by people that produced a model small enough for a laptop. The company emerged from stealth in May with $650 million in funding at a $4.65 billion valuation, from backers including GV, Nvidia, and AMD Ventures. Recursive is led by CEO Richard Socher, Salesforce’s former chief scientist. Because Flint runs on a user’s own computer rather than a company’s cloud servers, developers can use it offline, keep their code private, and avoid the usage fees that AI cloud services charge based on how much text the model processes. The model is free to download on Hugging Face, the popular site for sharing AI models, under the Apache 2.0 license, an open source license that allows free use and modification. Flint is a mixture-of-experts model, meaning it uses only a small slice of itself for any given task: just 2.5 billion of its 40 billion settings, known as parameters, at a time. That makes it light enough for an ordinary laptop and far smaller than Meta’s Muse Spark Open , an open model built for Macs that was released last week. Muse Spark Open uses 816 billion parameters and needs at least a terabyte of memory. Flint is also fast. In Recursive’s tests, it generated about 131 tokens (chunks of text) per second on a MacBook Pro with Apple’s M4 Pro chip — roughly twice the 58 to 69 tokens per second that similar models managed on the same machine, including Google’s Gemma 4 and Nvidia’s Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. On Nvidia’s RTX Spark, Flint topped 150 tokens per second. On SWE-Bench Verified, a benchmark that measures how well AI can fix real-world software bugs, Flint outperformed other models under 50 billion parameters. On Recursive’s own average across six tests, only one model, Alibaba’s Qwen3.8 27B, scored higher than Flint. The company acknowledged that Flint would need more guidance than the big paid coding assistants and suggested breaking large tasks into smaller steps. Still, early reviews were positive. Wired’s Will Knight used Flint on a Mac with 48GB of memory to build several small programs, including a to-do list app and a tool that scours the web for research. He found that smaller coding models often ran into errors or were slow compared to Claude or Codex, but Flint nailed his coding requests every time. The Eureka Machine comes up with ideas, runs experiments, and uses the results to decide what to try next. According to the company’s launch video , it contributed to nearly every part of building Flint, from pretraining to post-training and inference. Recursive said that Eureka’s contributions include a sparser model shape, low-bit training that shrank Flint by 71% with almost no loss in quality and custom kernels, which are specialized programs that speed up the underlying computations. Recursive didn’t say how much time the Eureka Machine saved its researchers, but it’s not alone in leaning on AI to do research. OpenAI said last month that by mid-August, its AI agents were logging 3.1 workdays for every one worked by a human researcher.

articles.title: Automattic begins layoffs following board upheaval and executive departures | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Sources say more cuts could follow as the company looks to improve its finances.
articles.body_text: Automattic, the parent company to WordPress.com , WooCommerce, Tumblr, and others, has begun layoffs, and insiders tell us they are bracing for more cuts to come. Over at least the past week, the cuts have impacted its communications team, social team, WordPress.com, and its VIP enterprise business. The departures represent more turmoil at Automattic, whose team is still reeling from the board’s failed attempt to oust CEO Matt Mullenweg in September, resulting in a complete board turnover and other exec departures, including its CFO, interim CFO , and chief legal officer. Automattic’s director of communications, Megan Fox, posted about her departure last week on LinkedIn, saying the move was an “unexpected end” and that her role had been “eliminated.” Meanwhile, after TechCrunch reported that Automattic’s interim CFO Jeremy Klaperman left earlier this month , only weeks after the board shake-up, Mullenweg posted on X suggesting Klaperman may have been “offended” by the company’s decision to seek external candidates to fill the role. (Internally, however, Mullenweg had asked Klaperman to reconsider leaving, we had heard.) At one point, Mullenweg also shared personal information about one of the recently departed execs in the company’s internal Slack, according to screenshots viewed by TechCrunch. The post was related to a health matter impacting the person’s spouse and claimed that the company was not providing this person with much-needed COBRA insurance. Mullenweg said the exec was threatening to sue over this. Mullenweg also shared that his own fiancée had been impacted by the same health condition. Some employees told us they were shocked that the CEO would share something so private and personal in such a forum. Throughout this month, TechCrunch has heard from different sources that members of Automattic’s team have also been let go, including those in marketing and product at WordPress.com. Reached for comment about the layoffs last week, Mullenweg said the terminations were not above its normal numbers. Asked on Wednesday about the growing total, Mullenweg said that today he was “mostly focused on PHP.” (He posted on X about the PHP security issue hitting the internet, which is taking priority.) The company’s About page lists the total number of staff at 1,397, but insiders tell us that the plan is likely to spread out the layoffs over the months ahead, in the hopes of improving Automattic’s Q4 revenue figures ahead of a debt renegotiation that’s coming up in June. In a statement shared with TechCrunch, Automattic spokesperson Chenda Ngak said, “We’re staggering our organizational changes to be more generous with severance and allow more time with each Automattician.” Updated after publication with Automattic’s statement. articles.title: The internet is having a very bad cybersecurity day | TechCrunch
articles.summary: From AI-discovered PHP vulnerabilities to flaws in Node.js and popular AI tool LiteLLM, cybersecurity teams have plenty to worry about this week.
articles.body_text: The internet is having a bad day, from a cybersecurity perspective. Government websites around the world went offline , Reuters reported, after AI discovered critical security vulnerabilities that impacted the programming language PHP . The issues were severe enough that the U.S. National Security Agency (NSA) advised organizations using PHP on their systems to either immediately update or take their systems offline until they could. But the PHP update wasn’t the only headache cybersecurity folks were facing on Wednesday. Node.js , the open source JavaScript runtime environment, also dropped a security surprise of its own when it shared that four high-severity vulnerabilities were just patched in its latest release. One allowed remote code execution, and two others would have permitted a TLS validation bypass, potentially allowing attackers to bypass checks intended to verify a server’s identity. In addition, LiteLLM, a popular open source proxy for routing requests to multiple LLM providers, was compromised by an attacker who injected malicious code, the company shared in a post on X on Wednesday afternoon. The malicious artifacts were published to PyPI (Python Package Index), Docker Hub , and GHCR (GitHub Container Registry), the post noted. The malicious code was said to include an information stealer that targeted cloud credentials, passwords, and AI service credentials, in addition to a remote access trojan that could allow hackers to execute commands on compromised systems. LiteLLM said it has now removed the malicious releases and images and advised anyone who installed them to follow the remediation guidance it provided. And wait, there’s more! An Indian certificate authority, eMudhra, had its private keys compromised , potentially allowing attackers to issue fraudulent certificates and impersonate legitimate websites. Security pros have called this a massive cleanup job and one that’s “bigger than Heartbleed.” (The latter is a reference to the critical security vulnerability in the OpenSSL cryptographic software library.) These issues come on the heels of other security breaches and hacks, including the breach of the cloud-native database-as-a-service, TiDB Cloud, which the company announced on Monday. Other hackers have been exploiting four patched Plex Media Server flaws, collectively called Plex2Shell. And last week, cybersecurity company BeyondTrust warned customers to patch a critical zero-day in its Remote Support product, which had been exploited since August. Though the issues were unrelated to each other, their back-to-back arrival highlights the challenges cybersecurity teams now face. This is particularly important as AI could make it easier for attackers to exploit vulnerabilities once discovered. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Mass Effect is Amazon’s next video game adaptation
articles.summary: According to a report from Variety, a tv show based on BioWare’s Mass Effect franchise is officially in development at Amazon MGM Studios.
articles.body_text: After its success with Fallout and the recently released Like A Dragon: Yakuza show, Mass Effect is the next game Amazon wants to adapt. According to Variety, a show based on BioWare’s military space opera RPG is officially in production at Amazon MGM Studios. Variety has reported that F9: The Fast Saga writer Daniel Casey has signed on to write the show with BioWare producer Mike Gamble serving as executive produce along with Ari Arad. Though BioWare released the Mass Effect Legendary Edition — a collection of the first three games updated for modern consoles — back in 2021, the Mass Effect series hasn’t had an original entry since the release of Mass Effect: Andromeda back in 2017. After Andromeda, BioWare released Anthem, a live-service action game that was significant departure from the studio’s tradition of making single-player, story-driven RPGs. In 2020, BioWare announced that a new Mass Effect game was in-development. News of a Mass Effect TV show comes on what is known as N7 Day, a semi-official, fan-created holiday that celebrates all things Mass Effect. On previous N7 Days, BioWare has teased information about the next game in the series including a trailer that possibly suggested the return of fan-favorite protagonist Commander Shepard whose story ended with the original trilogy. Though no story details have been revealed about the show, it’s a pretty safe bet to guess it’ll focus on the Commander and I personally can’t wait to see her.

How Big Tech is swallowing the AI industry
articles.summary: Amazon has replicated an antitrust-avoidance playbook pioneered by Microsoft with its hiring of most of the team behind buzzy AI startup Adept.
articles.body_text: A couple of months ago, I was sitting in the audience at a tech conference in San Fransisco watching Bloomberg’s Emily Chang interview Reid Hoffman. She asked about Microsoft’s hiring of the team behind Inflection, a would-be OpenAI competitor that Hoffman co-founded. It was an acquisition in everything but name, clearly designed to avoid the scrutiny of antitrust regulators. Not only had Microsoft (where Hoffman is a board member) hired most of Inflection’s employees — it also licensed the startup’s technology in a way that seemed designed to make its investors whole. Speaking with Chang that day onstage, Hoffman predicted that what happened to Inflection will become a “pattern” for future AI deals. We are seeing that pattern play out now. Last Friday, Amazon announced that it is hiring most of the team behind Adept, another would-be OpenAI competitor that raised about $400 million from top-tier investors to build, in the words of CEO David Luan, “a new type of giant model that turns natural language into actions on your machine.” Alexandra Miller, an Amazon spokesperson, told The Verge that the company had hired “close to” to 66 percent of Adept’s employees. In an internal memo published by GeekWire’s Taylor Soper, SVP Rohit Prasad said that, like Microsoft with Inflection, Amazon will also be licensing Adept’s technology to “accelerate our roadmap for building digital agents that can automate software workflows.” Adept’s corporate blog post about the news suggests it was running out of money: “Continuing with Adept’s initial plan of building both useful general intelligence and an enterprise agent product would’ve required spending significant attention on fundraising for our foundation models, rather than bringing to life our agent vision.” Recent reports say the company has been looking to sell itself. The reality is that building leading AI models is extremely costly, and raising $400 million isn’t even enough to compete these days. Big Tech, meanwhile, is flush with cash and looking to get in on what everyone perceives to be the next big thing. It’s logical for more AI startups to go the way of Inflection and Adept as the industry consolidates. The problem for Big Tech is that they are no longer allowed to buy companies like they once did. The current antitrust enforcement regime would most certainly try to block an Amazon acquisition of Adept, whether there is a strong legal argument for doing so or not. (Amazon execs are still seething about not being allowed to buy a robot vacuum cleaner company.) Even still, capitalism finds a way. What Microsoft did to Inflection, and what Amazon just did to Adept, is the new Big Tech playbook for swallowing the AI industry and getting away with it. Silicon Valley has a storied history of acquihires, where a startup is gutted for its people and left for dead. Microsoft and Amazon have done what are essentially reverse acquihires, where the hiring of people and a corresponding licensing deal is designed to disguise what is actually an acquisition. Reid Hoffman, meanwhile, should probably be congratulated for more than just an accurate prediction about the future of these deals — one of Adept’s earliest investors was none other than his venture capital firm, Greylock. Correction, July 1st: A previous version of this story incorrectly stated the percentage of Adept employees hired by Amazon. The percentage is “close to” 66 percent, not 80 percent.

articles.body_text: V:s kryssraket Mohamed Ali har varit tyst om det misstänkta valfusket kopplat till hans personvalskampanj i Borlänge. – Jag har inte blivit delgiven misstanke om något brott, säger han till SVT Nyheter . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. I dag är Mohamed Ali på plats i riksdagen för första gången sedan han kryssades in. – Jag har inte blivit delgiven misstanke om något brott. Jag kommer att behålla min plats i riksdagen och representera de människor som röstade på mig, säger han till SVT Nyheter. Han berättar att han kommer att behålla sin riksdagsplats. – Jag har inte hört någonting från polisen. Utöver det misstänkta valfusket har det även rapporterats att Ali har obetalade skulder hos Kronofogden, inte har betalat underhåll till sitt barn och hävdat att han har företag som inte finns. – Det känns bra att representera folk som gett mig förtroende och träffa arbetskamraterna i riksdagen. Men de senaste veckorna har varit påfrestande, säger Mohamed Ali. Enligt SVT välkomnar han att utredningen fortgår. Tidigare i dag framgick det, i handlingar från Falu tingsrätt, att tre personer misstänks i ärendet om valfusk i Borlänge. Enligt Ali är han inte en av de tre. Detta är en nyhetsartikel. articles.title: Efter it-larmet – experter varnar för ”våg av hackerattacker”
articles.summary: Miljontals sajter hotas av angrepp efter att en allvarlig säkerhetslucka upptäcktes under onsdagen. Nu varnar experter för en våg av hackerattacker och det rapporteras redan om miljontals angreppsförsök.
articles.body_text: Miljontals sajter hotas av attacker efter att en allvarlig säkerhetslucka upptäcktes under onsdagen. Nu varnar experter för en våg av hackerattacker. Och det rapporteras redan om miljontals angreppsförsök. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Experter varnar för en ”bredare våg” av hackerattacker efter att två säkerhetsbrister upptäcktes i programmeringsspråket php under onsdagen. 70 procent av världens sajter bygger på php, enligt marknadsundersökningsföretaget W3Techs . I Sverige handlar det om 330 000 aktiva hemsidor, enligt analysverktyget Builtwith . Alp Toker, cybersäkerhetsexpert på NetBlocks, kallar problemet ”mycket allvarligt” och varnar för att hackare nu kan utnyttja bristerna i php. – Det är början på en bredare våg av attacker, säger han till Sky News. Under onsdagseftermiddagen släpptes en uppdatering och myndighetssajter i länder som Finland, Danmark och Nederländerna valde att stänga ner i väntan på den. I Sverige uppmanade Nationellt cybersäkerhetscenter alla verksamheter att uppdatera sina system omgående, eller koppla bort dem från internet. Samtidigt innebär uppdateringen i sig en sårbarhet, enligt Alp Toker. – Nu när uppdateringen har släppts kan ai-agenter lära sig från den och återskapa attacken mycket lättare, säger han till Sky News .

articles.title: Samuel Jonsson: Mamdanikampanjen behöver inte vara Dadgostars
articles.summary: Moderaten Samuel Jonsson, Timbro, tycker att högerpartierna varit dåliga att locka storstadsväljare. Nu vill han vända trenden genom att kopiera Mamdani.
articles.body_text: Moderaten Samuel Jonsson, Timbro, tycker att högerpartierna varit för dåliga att locka storstadsväljare. Nu vill han vända trenden – genom att kopiera New Yorks borgmästare. – Mamdanikampanjen behöver inte vara Dadgostars, den kan lika gärna vara borgerlig. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Nyligen utsågs Samuel Jonsson, 28, till ledare för tankesmedjan Timbros nya satsning ”Högern och staden”. Han har flyttat till Stockholm från Lund, där han fram till nu varit aktiv inom Moderaterna och ungdomsförbundet Muf. I somras listades han av Expressen som en av landets unga makthavare . I sin nya roll ska han arbeta för att öka antalet högerväljare i svenska storstäder. – Tittar man på Stockholm, Göteborg och Malmö så är det rödare än någonsin, säger Jonsson. Redan nu har Samuel Jonsson en klar bild av vad som brustit. Fokuset på billigare drivmedel och sänkta elpriser, som gett många nya väljare på landsbygden där människor kör bil och bor i villa, har varit svårsålt i städer med kollektivtrafik och en befolkning som bor i lägenheter. – Och om man säger att man tappar i storstäderna för att Sverigedemokraterna är radioaktiva där, då gör man det för lätt för sig.

Åklagarmyndighetens riksenhet mot korruption har under flera veckor utrett misstänkt valfusk i Borlänge . Nu visar handlingar från Falu tingsrätt att tre personer ses som misstänkta i ärendet och att åklagaren, på torsdagen, har inkommit med ett förordnande om tre offentliga försvarare i målet. Det framgår inte vilka som är misstänkta, men brottsperioden för det misstänkta valfusket anges till den 26 augusti till 4 september. – Det är tre stycken framställningar som vi har skickat in till tingsrätten, det betyder att det är tre misstänka, säger åklagare Johan Lindmark till Expressen. Utredningen om misstänkt valfusk inleddes av Borlängepolisen redan under förtidsröstningen. Rubriceringen är otillbörligt verkande vid röstning. Två av de nu misstänkta som ska få offentliga försvarare misstänks för att ha påverkat valet, den ena av dessa misstänks för medhjälp. Den tredje misstänks för att ha tagit emot någon form av förmån. Rubriceringen för den personen är ”tagande av otillbörlig förmån vid röstning i Borlänge”. Den händelsen ska ha skett den 28 augusti.

articles.title: KD: ”Fruktbara” samtal med C
articles.summary: Sverige har varit utan regering i sex veckor. Nu uppger Busch att KD har ”fruktbara samtal” med C. – Det finns ett värde av att veta var man har varandra politiskt , säger hon på en pressträff.
articles.body_text: Ebba Busch och Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist har ”fruktbara samtal” om regeringsbildningen. – Det finns ett värde av att veta var man har varandra politiskt. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. C-ledaren Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist har fått i uppdrag att sondera förutsättningarna för att bilda en mittenregering. Det var ett klokt val av talmannen, uppger Ebba Busch (KD) på en pressträff. – Det är bra att pröva om det finns en möjlighet för en mittenorienterad regering eller någon annan konstellation och få frågan uttömd om det finns en väg framåt här, säger hon. Samtidigt poängterar hon att KD inte har några nya besked att ge om vem partiet vill se som statsminister eller vilken regering de vill se. – Men vi har ändå, menar jag, fruktbara samtal med i det här fallet Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist och Centerpartiet utifrån om vi skulle antingen ingå i en regering tillsammans, eller om vi från KD skulle sitta i opposition. Den regering som Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist sonderar för är med Magdalena Andersson (S) som statsminister. Busch menar dock att KD:s tidigare linjer kvarstår. – Kristdemokraterna har inte Magdalena Andersson som statsministerkandidat. Vi har inga nya besked att ge, det finns inga nya öppningar. Men däremot tror jag att det viktigt och fruktbart att vi ändå talar politik med varandra, säger hon. Koalitioner av olika slag har börjat bildas i Sverige sedan valet. Så sent som i går stod det klart att region Stockholm bildat ett blocköverskridande mittenstyre med S, MP, C, L och KD .

articles.title: En död på Stegra efter fall – sorgen
articles.summary: En person har dött på Stegras stålverksbygge i Boden efter att ha fallit från en höjd. Händelsen utreds som en arbetsplatsolycka.
articles.body_text: En person har dött i en arbetsplatsolycka på Stegra i Boden. – Det känns som jag har förlorat en familjemedlem, säger kollegan Daniel Ratiu, 24, från Rumänien. Nu ska bland annat Byggnads utreda händelsen. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Det var vid 11.30-tiden på onsdagen som polisen larmades till Stegras stålverksbygge i Norra Svartbyn, Boden. En person hade då fallit från en höjd. Efter olyckan har företaget gått ut med att personen omkommit, i kommunikation till medarbetarna. Polisen bekräftar att en man i 65-årsåldern, från ett annat europeiskt land, fallit från en plattform och omkommit. Händelsen utreds som vållande till annans död genom arbetsmiljöbrott. Polisen har bland annat dokumenterat olycksplatsen och hållit förhör med vittnen. Stegra skriver i ett pressmeddelande att omständigheterna kring dödsfallet ska undersökas av myndigheter och internt. ”Våra tankar går till personens familj, vänner och kolleger”, skriver företaget. När det kommer till just dödliga arbetsplatsolyckor i Sverige är byggarbetare överrepresenterade i statistiken. – Det är oerhört tragiskt, säger Claes Danell, ordförande för Byggnads i region norr, om olyckan. – Vi kan bara konstatera att ännu en gång har en byggnadsarbetare dött i vår bransch. Det dör ungefär en byggnadsarbetare i månaden. Det finns ingen annan bransch som är så utsatt för dödsfall.

articles.title: Aftonbladets chefredaktör lämnar: ”Jag väldigt stolt”
articles.summary: Aftonbladets chefredaktör Lotta Folcker lämnar posten. Informationen gavs till redaktionen vid ett extrainkallat stormöte på torsdagen.
articles.body_text: Aftonbladets chefredaktör Lotta Folcker lämnar posten. Informationen gavs till redaktionen vid ett extrainkallat stormöte på torsdagen. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Lotta Folcker tillträdde som chefredaktör och vd på Aftonbladet våren 2024. Hon efterträdde då Lena K Samuelsson. Nu lämnar Folcker uppdraget. Beskedet lämnades vid ett stormöte på Aftonbladets redaktion på torsdagsförmiddagen. – Jag är väldigt stolt över det vi har åstadkommit tillsammans och framför allt över alla otroligt fina och proffsiga människor som jobbar här och åstadkommer så mycket varje dag. Det är en sorg att lämna och Aftonbladet kommer alltid att ha en särskild plats i mitt hjärta, säger Lotta Folcker till egna tidningen . Lotta Folcker sjukskrevs tidigare under hösten. Aftonbladets redaktionschef Karin Schmidt har då fungerat som tillförordnad ansvarig utgivare för tidningen, har Dagens Media rapporterat. – På Aftonbladet finns många skickliga människor och en stor vilja att fortsätta utveckla mediehuset. Det ger oss goda förutsättningar att driva arbetet vidare, samtidigt som vi tar oss tid att hitta rätt person att leda Aftonbladet på längre sikt, säger Siv Juvik Tveitnes, koncernchef för ägaren Schibsted. Lotta Folcker kom till Aftonbladet 2014, men lämnade tidningen 2021 för att bli sportchef på Viaplay. Detta är en nyhetsartikel. articles.title: Misstänkt ryskt spionage: ”Inte haft en fisk ombord”
articles.summary: The Telegraphs granskning visar 500 händelser nära undervattensinfrastruktur och väcker oro för sabotage mot Storbritanniens viktiga nät
articles.body_text: Ryssland misstänks använda fisketrålare för att kartlägga brittiska undervattenskablar. En granskning av The Telegraph avslöjar över 500 misstänkta incidenter. – Vissa av de här fartygen har aldrig haft en enda fisk ombord, säger en Nato-källa till tidningen. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Tidningens granskning bygger på fyra och ett halvt års spårningsdata från satellittjänsten Global Fishing Watch. Totalt identifierades 17 ryska fartyg som under längre perioder rört sig långsamt i närheten av undervattenskablar. Enligt The Telegraph kan rörelsemönstren tyda på att fartygen kartlägger kablarnas exakta positioner. Kunskapen skulle kunna användas för att angripa infrastrukturen i en framtida konflikt med Nato. Kablarna transporterar stora mängder data mellan länder och är avgörande för bland annat banker, sjukhus, transporter och mobilnät. Om de slås ut kan konsekvenserna bli omfattande. En källa inom Nato uppger för The Telegraph att alliansen är medveten om de ryska fiskefartygens aktiviteter. – Vissa av de här fartygen har aldrig haft en enda fisk ombord, säger källan till The Telegraph. Enligt marina experter kan fartyg som rör sig mycket långsamt använda sonar för att kartlägga havsbotten. De kan också potentiellt använda fjärrstyrda undervattensfarkoster för att undersöka kablarna närmare. Samtidigt har oron för ryska angrepp mot undervattensinfrastruktur ökat. Den brittiska flottans chef, amiral Gwyn Jenkins, har varnat för att Ryssland skulle kunna angripa landets undervattenskablar redan från den första dagen av en konflikt med Nato. Den brittiska regeringen planerar nu att skärpa lagstiftningen för att skydda infrastrukturen. Förslagen omfattar nya brott och fängelsestraff på upp till 14 år för avsiktlig skadegörelse på undervattensinfrastruktur.
